name: Minnesota
source: Minnesota reader session (Stage 5 tools), 2026-11-19: the November 2026 Open States dump converted with scripts/stage5/openstates/; every floor roll call of a 736-bill dry batch (735 bills one topic's scan found, plus 2023 SF 2909 from the instrument store; 19 roll calls, 2020-2026) read from the House and Senate journals with the verifier's own fetch, and each member's vote compared with the dump where the dump holds one. One bill text was read for its marks (2018 HF 3762 as introduced); no text was measured in bulk.
sessions: The Legislature is numbered by biennium: the 90th 2017-2018, the 91st 2019-2020, the 92nd 2021-2022, the 93rd 2023-2024, the 94th 2025-2026. It meets in both years of the biennium, January to May. Open States names the regular sessions "2017-2018" and so on. Bill numbers run through the whole biennium and start again with the next Legislature: House files HF 1 up, Senate files SF 1 up, each with a companion in the other chamber (2023 SF 2909 and HF 2890). Special sessions are frequent (2017s1, 2019s1, seven in 2020, 2021s1, 2025s1); the Revisor files a special session's bills under the year it sat with its number (/bills/91/2020/4/HF/1/), and the journals of a special session sit in the biennium's folder. House 134 seats, Senate 67; each Senate district holds two House districts (A and B).
bill_data: No LegiScan dataset is on disk for Minnesota. Bills, sponsors and roll calls come from Open States data, converted to the same folder layout (MN-900125 to MN-900141: 2013-2014 and the regular and special sessions 2017-2018 to 2025s1; scripts/stage5/openstates/README.md). Each folder carries a .openstates.json; its ids are ours and no legiscan.com page exists for them.

The dump holds no roll call for 2020's special sessions, 2021-2022 or 2021's special session, and its 2017-2020 vote addresses are House pages that now answer 500. So no Minnesota dump vote is placed: scripts/stage5/openstates/fetch-legislature-rollcalls.ts reads each bill's page on the Revisor's site (/bills/<ls>/<year>/<ssn>/<HF|SF>/<num>/), keeps each chamber's row with a tally whose words are the passage or repassage of the bill ("Bill was passed", "Bill was repassed as amended by Conference", "Third reading Passed"), counts every motion and the other chamber's echo of a vote, and reads the vote from the journal page the row links to, through the chamber's page resolver; convert.py places only those (record_is_the_floor) and keeps every other dump vote marked committee, with the reason in _openstates.not_placed. Run the fetch for every bill the scan finds, session by session, then convert the whole state again.

Compared 2026-11-19: 19 floor roll calls read from the record, 0 refused (2019-2020 2, 2021-2022 2, 2023-2024 9, 2025-2026 6). The 80 scanned bills of 2017-2018 and the 11 of the special sessions had no floor vote with a tally. 7 roll calls have no dump copy. Of the other 12, 6 were settled by the tally among several on one day and 1 sits a day later in the dump than in the journal (2023 SF 2909's House repassage: journal 2023-05-15, dump 05-16). Tally differences: 0. Member votes compared: 1,374, differences: 0. Every dump label fit one record name once two former names were read (below).

The journals print family names, with initials where two members share one ("Anderson, P. E.", "Lee, K."), so the reader takes the Legislative Reference Library's member list for that Legislature and chamber (www.lrl.mn.gov/legdb/results?search=session&gender=all&sess=93&body=house) as a second document and maps each label to the one member it fits. A label printed under a former or legal name the list does not show is named through MN_LABEL_ALIASES in src/lib/stateRollCallEvidence.ts, each entry an LRL id checked on the member's detail page: "O'Neill" (Marion Rarick, 2017-2024), "Lee, K." (Liz Lee, legal name Kaozouapa Elizabeth Lee, 2023-2026), "Kunesh-Podein" (Mary Kunesh) and "Neu" (Anne Neu Brindley), both 2020. A label that fits no member, or two, is kept as printed and gives no line. Roster legislators: 200 (133 House, 67 Senate), all linked. 191 linked by name match; 13 idmap lines by hand: 9 sitting members the datasets hold under a short name or a nickname (Ripper Repinski, Mike Howard, Huldah Hiltsley and others), 3 people the converter made from the journal's full name (Patricia Anderson twice, Huldah Momanyi-Hiltsley), and Brad Tabke's 2019-2020 id.

votes.floor_rule: A vote is cited as the journal page that prints it, with the page and the bill after a #: the House's day page www.house.mn.gov/cco/journals/<2023-24>/J<MMDD><day>.htm#Page<page>-<SF2934>, the Senate's day PDF www.mnsenate.gov/journals/<2023-2024>/<YYYYMMDD><day>.pdf#Page<page>-<SF2909>. The page tells apart two votes on one bill on one day. The House journal prints the bill's heading ("S. F. No. 2934, A bill for an act ..."), "The bill was read for the third time", the question with its tally ("The question was taken on the passage of the bill and the roll was called. There were 70 yeas and 60 nays as follows:"), the yea and nay groups, and the result ("The bill was passed, as amended, and its title agreed to."). The Senate journal prints "S.F. No. 2909 was read the third time, as amended, and placed on its final passage.", the question, "The roll was called, and there were yeas 34 and nays 33, as follows:", the groups in columns (each may be followed by a Rule 40 paragraph naming members for whom another senator cast the vote), and "So the bill passed and its title was agreed to." The reader (src/lib/stateRollCallEvidence.ts) reads a vote only when the question is the passage or repassage of the bill, the bill read is the address's bill, the address's page lies between the reading and the last name, each group lists the count the tally prints, every page banner or running head gives the address's day and chamber, the House day's heading names the Legislature or special session, and the line after the last group is the bill's result. The journals list only those voting yea and nay; a member who did not vote is in neither group and gets no line. The Senate adopts a conference committee's report by one roll call and repasses the bill by the next; the repassage is the floor vote and the adoption is counted as a motion. Committee votes, amendments, calls of the House or Senate, appeals of the chair's ruling and every other motion are not mapped.
gaps: Committee votes, votes on amendments, the adoption of a conference committee's report, motions to recall a bill or suspend the rules, appeals of the chair's ruling and calls of the House or Senate are not votes on the bill and are not mapped (runner, 2026-11-16). The dump holds 47 such votes on the dry batch's bills.
A member who did not vote is not listed by the journal: no line, never a Yea or a Nay.

A label that fits no member of that Legislature's LRL list, or two, gives no line. None remained in the dry batch once four former or legal names were added as aliases; a new one must be checked on the member's LRL detail page ("Former Name", "Legal Name") before it is added.

The keyword scan reads a bill's short title, and an omnibus bill's title names no topic (2023 SF 2909, "Omnibus Judiciary and Public Safety appropriations", whose 20 articles its title does not name). Such a bill reaches a run only through the instrument store; its floor votes must then be fetched by naming it (fetch-legislature-rollcalls.ts --bills-file).

texts.marks: Read on 1 text (2018 HF 3762 as introduced; 2026-11-19). In a bill that amends existing law, words added are UNDERLINED (<ins>) and words deleted are STRUCK THROUGH (class del, line-through). The page also carries screen-reader words around each mark, so plain text keeps them as "new text begin ... new text end" and "deleted text begin ... deleted text end": a quote copied from the plain text must leave those words out and must not quote a deleted passage as the law. Each line carries its page and line number ("1.1", "1.2") in the margin.
texts.note: The dump links each version as www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/text.php?number=HF3762&version=0&session=ls90&session_year=2018&session_number=0, which redirects to /bills/<ls>/<year>/<ssn>/<HF|SF>/<num>/versions/<v>/; the same address serves a PDF of the version. A bill's page /bills/<ls>/<year>/<ssn>/<HF|SF>/<num>/ redirects to the year the bill was introduced (the 94th's HF 3433 is /94/2026/0/), and lists each chamber's actions with the journal page and tally of each recorded vote.

search_note: Minnesota sponsorships and House and Senate floor votes for 2017 to 2026 come from the bill data on disk, checked against the Legislature's own journals: skip the Revisor's bill pages and the journals, and add the place "sponsor list: covered by bulk bill data". Many provisions pass inside omnibus bills whose titles do not name them (2023 SF 2909): check the instrument store for such a bill before deciding a person has no vote on the topic. Spend the search on their own words (statements, campaign pages, newsletters, floor remarks, interviews, questionnaires). If any page returns 403, 429, an empty page or a bot check, record it as blocked and move on: do not retry it with a different user agent, headers or tool.
bill_table_note:
- Minnesota's Legislature is numbered by biennium (the 93rd is 2023-2024); bill numbers run through both years (HF 1, SF 1 up) and each bill has a companion in the other chamber.
- Floor votes kept: the passage and the repassage of a bill. Committee votes, amendments, a conference committee report's adoption and other motions are not floor votes on the bill.
- Texts: UNDERLINED words are added to existing law; STRUCK-THROUGH words are deleted. Plain text keeps them as "new text begin ... new text end" and "deleted text begin ... deleted text end": never quote a deleted passage as the law.
quirks: robots.txt states no crawl delay on www.revisor.mn.gov, www.house.mn.gov, www.mnsenate.gov or www.lrl.mn.gov. The reader waits one second between requests. No 403, 429 or bot check was met on 2026-11-19.

One vote needs the day's journal (a House day page is 1-2 MB of Word HTML; a Senate day PDF 100-300 KB) and the LRL member list (about 150-250 KB). The line tool took 20 seconds for 200 random votes from an empty page cache (19 journals).

The Revisor's bill page names a journal page, not a day: each chamber's page resolver names the day's file. The Senate's (www.mnsenate.gov/api/journal/gotopage?page=5105&ls=93) answers JSON; the House's (www.house.mn.gov/scripts/gotopage.pl?session=ls93&number=7097) answers a redirect, refuses some pages over HTTP/2 (HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED) and ends its Location header with a bare newline.

The House journal is Word HTML: windows-1252 to 2024, utf-8 in 2026. Its page banner changed in 2026 from "Journal of the House - 56th Day - Tuesday, April 25, 2023 - Top of Page 7013" to "Journal Of the House -  63rd -Thursday, April 23, 2026 - Top of Page 6145", with "<a name = 6145>". A House special session's days share the biennium's folder and number from one; the day's heading ("FOURTH SPECIAL SESSION - 2020") tells them apart.

The Senate journal's running heads alternate: odd pages "49TH DAY] FRIDAY, APRIL 14, 2023 5105", even pages "5106 JOURNAL OF THE SENATE [49TH DAY". A call of the Senate can sit between the third reading and the question (2026 SF 4067); 2026 writes "read the third time and placed" with no comma. Page numbers on the Revisor's page may carry a leading "+" (2025).
The Open States dump stores some names as UTF-8 read as Latin-1 ("PÃ©rez-Vega"; 893 vote labels). The record's names come from the LRL list and are not affected.
A House session can run past midnight: the journal dates the day it opened, and the dump may file a vote a day later (2023 SF 2909's repassage).
